app/src/lib/queries.ts:362-364 — data layer uses only stable query()/"use server"; no Nitro-specific APIs (no presets, route rules, cached handlers) leak into app code
app/src/app.tsx:1-46 and app/src/routes/* — no experimental config flags or API usage anywhere in the 14 source files (grep for preload/clientOnly/action/ssr/unstable_ found nothing)

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:3-9 — nitro() is SolidStart v2's only documented portable production runtime (docs.solidjs.com deployment-plugins), so the beta buys something no stable package provides

app/package.json:13 — exact pin 3.0.260610-beta skips the Sep 3 2026 security-hardening beta and the RC; the framework docs say npm i nitro (latest), so the frozen old beta is a needless, gratuitous risk
justification.rationale: Using Nitro 3 is unavoidable for a portable SolidStart v2 build and fully justified; the choice to freeze an exact June beta rather than track the RC adds risk without buying anything.

findings.issue: nitro is exactly pinned to 3.0.260610-beta (Jun 10 2026). Nitro 3 has since shipped a security-hardening beta (Sep 3 2026) and is now at release-candidate (3.0.261029-rc) with documented beta→RC breaking changes; the pin also means upgrades never happen automatically.
findings.suggestion: Track the current RC via a caret range or follow the framework docs (npm i nitro) and re-lock, then re-verify the build/start scripts against the RC before deploying.

findings.issue: The beta Nitro transitively pins rc/alpha dependencies (h3 2.0.1-rc.22, unstorage 2.0.0-alpha.7, ofetch 2.0.0-alpha.3, unenv 2.0.0-rc.24), widening the pre-stable surface beyond the one direct dependency.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable while SolidStart v2 mandates Nitro 3; note these in dependency-audit tooling and revisit when Nitro 3.0 final ships.

findings.issue: The whole framework stack is recently-stable (SolidStart 2 stable Aug 2026, Router 1.0 Jul 2026, Vite 8 Mar 2026), so breaking-change exposure is elevated for the next year even though nothing is experimental per se.
findings.suggestion: Keep the lockfile committed (it is) and pin engines (already done: node >=24, matching SolidStart v2's requirement) so upgrades are deliberate.

summary: The app itself is conservative: every route, component and query uses long-stable Solid/SolidStart APIs with zero experimental flags. The only pre-stable element is beta Nitro 3, which SolidStart v2's stable release effectively mandates as its portable production runtime, and it is perfectly contained in one vite.config.ts plugin line. The one real risk is the exact pin to a four-month-old beta that misses a security-hardening release and the current RC; otherwise this is a well-judged, low-experimental codebase.
